content:
On Friday last week (the 21st), during the verdict in the Hong Kong Alliance case, police took a woman who was queuing to observe the hearing into custody and removed her in a police vehicle in the early hours. Police responded to enquiries stating that the woman was arrested on three charges: "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent."

Around 5 a.m. that Friday, more than 50 people were already queuing outside the West Kowloon Magistrates' Courts. During the wait, a plainclothes police officer indicated that a woman in the queue was "suspected of wearing clothing with seditious intent," and took her away in a police vehicle. As officers led the woman away, several officers continuously directed journalists to leave, saying "take you to the press area," and pulled an orange cordon line towards Yam Wa Street. After the woman boarded the police vehicle, they put away the cordon line. A "court observation volunteer" queuing near the woman that day said she was wearing a black T-shirt with Japanese characters printed on it.

The Collective Media (集誌社) enquired with the police about the reason for the woman's removal and whether she had been arrested. Police replied this morning (the 24th) that during a security operation in the vicinity of the West Kowloon Courts on August 21, a 45-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of "disorderly conduct in a public place," "resisting or wilfully obstructing a police officer in the execution of duty," and "seditious intent," and was detained for investigation.
